# Enter-to-end-turn browser wait exceeds the 60 s hook above ~2x CPU oversubscription

## Headline

The `turn to advance after end-of-turn presentation` wait in
`tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` is already at the largest
budget the 60 s browser hook permits (40 000 ms = 16 000 ms cap + 24 000 ms
margin + 20 000 ms boot = 60 000 ms), yet it fails at ≈2× CPU oversubscription
because the bounded end-of-turn deferral is re-polled on Phaser's clamped game
clock, so the forced day start is detected late. **Decision: make the
deferral's safety cap starvation-proof** — one extracted helper whose deadline
and re-poll run on wall clock, enforced even while the page is not painting
(producer, Q1 = C, Q2 = 1).

## Problem statement

The soak evidence on MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L shows the gate passes 20/20 quiet
(peak load 15.3), passes 2/2 at 8 burners (peak 23.6), and fails exactly one
wait — `turn to advance after end-of-turn presentation` — at load ≥ ≈31
(≈2× oversubscription, 16 burners, peak 32.8). That wait's budget is already at
the ceiling the 60 s hook permits, so no poll-budget tweak inside the hook can
rescue it.

Root cause (mechanism, verified against the installed `phaser` source):
Phaser's `TimeStep` clamps the per-frame delta it feeds scenes — under
`smoothStep` (default on) each frame contributes at most `1000/fps.min`
(200 ms) — and `Clock.elapsed`, which drives `delayedCall` timers and tween
progress, advances by that clamped delta. Under starvation (a few frames per
second) all game-time-paced choreography stretches: income phase gaps, coin
flights, the incident hold, and the deferral's own 250 ms `delayedCall`
re-polls. The deferral *deadline* (`s.time.now + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`,
where `s.time.now` is the raw frame timestamp) is wall-clock, but it is only
re-checked at those clamped polls, so the forced day start is delayed by the
same starvation. Aggregate: closing choreography (stretched) + 16 s cap
(late-detected) + boot > the 40 s budget and the 60 s hook.

The cap's stated purpose is "end-of-turn can never hang the game"
(CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q, AC5/AC7). A stall bound that is only observed at frame
boundaries does not provide that guarantee — which is what this item fixes,
without touching the user-visible pacing.

## Users

- **Agent-implementer / gate runner** on the shared dev host: needs the browser
  gate green; a red `MainStreetScene` suite at ≈2× oversubscription burns whole
  sessions on retries and blocks the build → test → commit order.
- **Maintainer triaging a red browser suite**: needs a red wait to mean a
  behavioural regression, not host weather.
- **Release engineer** on the dev-push gate: a red gate on a loaded shared host
  stalls shipping even when the scene is correct.
- **Players**: unchanged pacing — the choreography, the incident hold and the
  cap value all stay as shipped; only the cap's *enforcement* becomes
  wall-clock rather than frame-clock, so under starvation the day advances at
  the documented bound instead of stalling past it.

Example user stories:

> As an agent running the browser gate on the shared 16-core host, I want the
> Enter-to-end-turn wait to pass at any load the host actually reaches, so that
> my gate result does not depend on which sibling suites happen to be running.

> As a player whose machine is momentarily overloaded, I want the end-of-turn
> to still advance within the documented safety window, so that the game can
> never appear hung.

## Existing state

- Measured envelope (2026-10-24, 16-core shared host): quiet 20/20 pass
  (peak 15.3); 8 burners 2/2 pass, then one fail at ambient 31.3; 16 burners
  fail at the 40 000 ms end-of-turn budget. Every other wait in the file passes
  at that load.
- The wait's effective budget is `capMs: INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` (16 000) +
  `floorMs: END_TURN_STARVATION_MARGIN_MS` (24 000) = 40 000 ms, the largest
  that keeps the documented 20 000 ms scene-boot allowance inside the 60 s
  `testTimeout` (asserted by `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts`). The
  suite's per-test timeout is already `it(..., 60_000)`.
- Five deferral polls race the choreography, all with the same shape
  (`startAt = <scene clock> + cap`, then `delayedCall(250, poll)`):
  3 in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` (`advanceTurn` ~433,
  forced event-choice ~617, piggyback ~783) and 2 in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` (`finish`'s income wait
  ~254 and the reveal gating ~301).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` already has the
  degradation precedent: `scheduleOrRun` runs the callback immediately when the
  scene has no clock (headless), which a wall-clock helper must preserve.
- Node unit suites drive these polls through fake `time` stubs
  (`tests/main-street/competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/turnflow.test.ts`), and
  `tests/main-street/income-collection-cap.test.ts` pins "exactly three
  `s.time.now + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` sites" by regex — both must be
  updated by the extraction.
- Reduced motion clears `incomeCollectionActive` synchronously in
  `MainStreetAnimatorIncome` (~line 1039), but it is **not** the remedy chosen:
  the parent rejected it as the sole remedy because it removes the
  deferred-income path from coverage.

## Desired change (decision: option C)

Replace the five duplicated deferral polls with **one shared, injectable
helper** that:

1. computes its deadline from a wall-clock timestamp (`Date.now()`),
2. re-polls with a wall-clock timer (`window.setTimeout`), not the scene clock,
3. forces completion (clearing `incomeCollectionActive` and invoking the
   caller's continuation) once `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` of wall time has
   elapsed since the deferral began,
4. is enforced even when the page is not painting — a backgrounded/hidden
   document ahead of the cap forces the advance rather than waiting for the
   next animation frame (Q2 = 1), and
5. degrades to today's behaviour where no clock/timer exists (headless node
   scenes run the continuation immediately), and exposes its clock/timer for
   deterministic unit driving.

Options considered and rejected (recorded for traceability):

- **A — accept and document the envelope** (no code change): the gate can still
  go red on the shared host when ambient load spikes ≥2×, conflicting with the
  "red tree never pushed" policy; rejected in favour of a root-cause fix.
- **B — reduced-motion Enter test + a separate cheap deferral-contract test**:
  no production change, but downgrades the file's end-to-end end-of-turn test
  to a synthetic and couples coverage to a reduced-motion implementation
  detail; retained only as a fallback if C's soak does not pass.
- **D — raise the browser hook for this test**: pure masking, requires
  amending the parent's "any derived budget must leave headroom for boot plus
  teardown within that hook" AC and re-baselining the guard's headroom rule,
  and would fail again at ≈4× oversubscription; rejected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **One bounded-deferral helper, wall-clock enforced.** All five
      income-collection deferral polls route through a single shared helper
      whose deadline is wall clock and whose re-poll is a wall timer; no inline
      `s.time.delayedCall(250, <poll>)` / `<scene clock> + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`
      poll remains. A unit test with a frozen scene clock and an advancing wall
      clock proves the continuation is forced within one poll interval of the
      16 000 ms cap.
- [ ] **Forced advance is not tied to paint.** When the document is hidden / no
      frame runs, the cap still forces the advance after the cap elapses
      (Q2 = 1). A unit test asserts the wall timer — not the scene clock —
      drives the assertion, and the behaviour is documented in the module's
      code comment.
- [ ] **Injectable and backward-compatible.** The helper accepts an injectable
      clock/timer (so `competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts`,
      `turnflow.test.ts` and the new tests drive it deterministically) and
      preserves today's no-clock degradation (headless scenes run the
      continuation immediately).
- [ ] **Single source of truth for the cap.** `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` stays
      16 000 and remains the only cap value; the
      `tests/main-street/income-collection-cap.test.ts` "exactly three
      `s.time.now + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` sites" pin is updated to the
      helper extraction (asserting the helper consumes the constant), so the
      duplication cannot silently return.
- [ ] **No production pacing change.** The choreography timing constants
      (`INCOME_PHASE_GAP_MS`, flight/stagger durations, `INCIDENT_REVEAL_HOLD_MS`)
      and the cap value are unchanged — pinned by existing/added unit tests;
      only the cap's enforcement mechanism differs.
- [ ] **Wait-budget guard still green.** `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts`
      passes unchanged: the end-of-turn wait keeps its cap-derived 40 000 ms
      budget and `budget + 20 s boot ≤ 60 s` headroom rule. If the soak shows
      the budget can now be reduced, that reduction is a *derived* margin
      change proved by the soak, not a hand-picked literal.
- [ ] **Reliability proven, not assumed.** `/skill:test --type soak-load`
      (≥ `nproc` burners) passes with the change, and the pre-change failure at
      the same burner count is reproduced and recorded on this item; both
      before/after tables (burners, peak load, runs, wall times, summary paths)
      are posted as a comment.
- [ ] **Documentation updated.** `docs/dev/testing.md` "Measured envelope" and
      the headroom rule section record the decision (cap enforced on wall
      clock, hidden-tab semantics) and the post-fix envelope, replacing the
      "above ~2× is outside the envelope" caveat with measured evidence; the
      helper's module comment documents the wall-clock contract. All related
      documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments,
      README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes
      (`/skill:test --type full`), evidence recorded on this item.

## Constraints

- **No behavioural change to production pacing.** The choreography, the
  incident hold and the cap value are shipped features
  (CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ, CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q); only the cap's enforcement may
  change.
- The parent's headroom constraint stands: `budget + scene-boot allowance` must
  stay inside the browser 60 s hook.
- Reduced motion must not become the sole remedy (parent decision); the
  deferred-income path keeps explicit coverage.
- All five deferral sites must keep identical semantics after extraction, and
  the existing fake-clock unit suites must not be weakened to accommodate the
  change.
- A stale wall timer must never fire into a destroyed scene — reuse the
  existing `scene.isActive()` / try-catch defensive pattern from the deferred
  closing tail.
- Agent-initiated test runs go through the test skill only
  (`/skill:test --type soak-load`, `--type full`); no ad-hoc `npx vitest` loops.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` — add the shared
  wall-clock deferral helper (sibling to `scheduleOrRun` ~line 176); adopt it in
  `finish`'s income wait (~254) and the reveal gating (~301).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — three deferral sites
  (`advanceTurn` ~433, forced event-choice ~617, piggyback ~783) adopt the
  helper.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorTiming.ts` — `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`
  unchanged; comment updated to state the wall-clock enforcement contract.
- `tests/main-street/income-collection-cap.test.ts` — the "exactly three
  `s.time.now + cap` sites" regex pin moves to the helper extraction.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/turnflow.test.ts` — fake `time` stubs: drive the injected
  timer/clock.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` — Enter test and its
  40 000 ms margin expected unchanged.
- `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts` — headroom rule re-check (expected
  unchanged).
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — "Measured envelope" + headroom rule: record the
  decision and the post-fix soak evidence.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the clamped-delta mechanism is the dominant starvation link
  and the deferral's poll cadence is the part that can be fixed without touching
  pacing. Verified against the installed Phaser source
  (`TimeStep.smoothDelta`, `Clock.now` / `Clock.elapsed` semantics); the
  before/after `soak-load` run is the confirmation.
- **Risk:** removing the late-detection link may not be sufficient on its own —
  the choreography phases before/after the deferral still stretch under
  clamped delta. Mitigation: the soak is a hard AC; if it still fails, the
  fallback is option B's separate deferral-contract test (not option D), and
  the residual envelope is re-documented with evidence.
- **Risk (accepted, decided):** a wall-clock cap changes hidden/backgrounded-tab
  behaviour — the day start is now forced after the cap instead of stalling
  until the tab paints again (Q2 = 1). This is the intended semantics of a stall
  bound; documented in the module comment and `docs/dev/testing.md`.
- **Risk:** a wall timer outliving the scene could fire into a destroyed scene.
  Mitigation: `scene.isActive()` guard plus the existing try-catch pattern; a
  unit test covers the destroyed/stale case.
- **Risk (scope creep):** the attractor is "rework all game-time animation off
  clamped delta" (tweens, phase gaps, incident hold). Explicitly out of scope —
  record as linked work items rather than expanding this one.

## Related work

- MS-0MVMKEU2000639TG — this item (`discovered-from:` the soak child
  MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L; soak evidence and envelope recorded there and in
  `docs/dev/testing.md` "Measured envelope").
- MS-0MVK2ACLN004VVIJ — parent: made the file's waits load-tolerant via
  cap-derived budgets; its headroom AC and "Measured limit (triaged, not a
  flake)" section are the origin of this item.
- MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L — the 20-run / under-load soak whose evidence defines the
  envelope and whose `soak-load` profile proves this fix.
- MS-0MVLINWV10005H2P — the wait-budget guard and headroom rule this item must
  keep green.
- MS-0MUYFX7Q2004JQ5R — shared end-of-turn closing presentation primitive that
  carries `incomeCollectionCapMs`.
- CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ / CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q — phased income choreography and
  deferred income window (untouched pacing; the property the cap protects).
- MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41 (open) — planned End-of-Turn summary dialog on the
  closing completion path; it will interact with the deferral this item
  extracts, so check dependency direction during planning.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L** – Prove browser-wait reliability: 20-run soak plus under-load run (completed)
- **MS-0MVLINWV10005H2P** – Guard browser wait budgets against production caps (completed)
- **MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** – End of Turn summary… (open; planned dialog on the closing path)

### Related repository files
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — engine developer guide; frame-loop/delta context.
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — measured envelope and headroom rule this item updates.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — documents reduced motion, deferral pacing and
  presentation behaviour these waits must respect.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Given the measured envelope (the gate fails only above ≈2× CPU
  oversubscription, load ≥ ~31), which remediation should this item
  implement — (A) accept and document the envelope with no code change,
  (B) convert the Enter test to reduced motion plus a separate cheap
  deferral-contract test, (C) make the income-collection deferral cap
  starvation-proof (wall-clock deadline + wall-clock poll, one extracted
  helper, production change confined to the safety cap), or (D) raise the
  browser hook for this test (parent AC amendment needed)?"
  — Answer (producer): **C** — make the income-collection deferral cap
  starvation-proof. Source: interactive reply (intake interview round 1,
  2026-10-25). Agent recommendation was C (stated with rationale before the
  answer); A was recorded as the zero-production-change fallback and B's second
  variant as the fallback if C's soak still fails. Research behind the
  recommendation: Phaser `TimeStep.smoothDelta` clamps per-frame delta to
  `1000/fps.min` (200 ms default), so under rAF starvation the choreography and
  the deferral's 250 ms `delayedCall` re-polls both run at a fraction of
  wall-clock speed — the wall-clock cap deadline is therefore detected late,
  which is the link C removes.
- Q2 (conditional on C): "Should the 16 000 ms cap be enforced against wall
  clock even when the page is not painting/visible (backgrounded tab or fully
  starved rAF — the day start is forced after 16 s wall even though the
  choreography never ran), or should the forced advance hold while the document
  is hidden/blurred and resume on visibility change?"
  — Answer (producer): **as recommended** = enforce on wall clock (option 1):
  the cap is a stall bound, nothing is visible while hidden, and today a hidden
  tab already stalls the animator indefinitely. Source: interactive reply
  (intake interview round 1, 2026-10-25). Recorded as an accepted, documented
  semantic change in the Risks section and to be reflected in the helper's
  module comment and `docs/dev/testing.md`.

# Decouple the storyline doc-drift guard from engine-owned heading text

**Headline:** `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts` AC5b pins literal Markdown headings of the engine-owned reference `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md` (a git submodule that dev builds advance to the engine's latest dev tip), so any engine-side heading rename silently reddens this game's unit suite. Replace the heading pins with semantic anchors (API symbols, link resolution) plus a rename-tolerant section-structure check, and document why headings are not a cross-repo contract.

discovered-from: MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L

## Problem statement

Dev builds (`npm run build` → `engine:sync`) compose the **latest** engine dev tip via `git submodule update --remote core`, not the pinned release SHA. When core (dev tip `01d6bcc1`) renamed `## Engine adapter` → `## Authoring seams (content, manifest, validator, author)` in `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md`, the game's doc-drift guard (AC5b) reddened on **every** dev build, for **every** game repo that pins those headings — even though nothing in Main Street changed. The inline fix (commit `9f2c6185`) asserted the new heading, but the underlying coupling remains: a heading is an implementation detail of the engine's prose, not a contract the game depends on.

## Users / user stories

- As a **Main Street developer**, when I bump or dev-sync the engine, I want `npm test` to fail only for genuine breakage, so a green suite is trustworthy and a red suite means something real.
- As a **release engineer**, I want the doc guard to still fail loudly if the engine reference the game's adapters link to disappears or stops documenting the seam API, so releases cannot silently ship against vanished docs.
- As the **producer/operator**, I want the cross-repo doc dependency to be explicit and cheap to maintain, so a rename is a no-op (or a documented one-line change), not a cross-repo firefight.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — No literal engine heading pins.** The AC5b block in `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts` no longer asserts literal section-heading text of `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md`; instead it asserts the semantic anchors the game genuinely depends on: the core reference exists, documents `createStorylineSystem` and the `@story-line` package, and names the `GymStorylineScene` consumer (any of these removed → guard fails).
- **AC2 — Rename tolerance is proven by a fixture test.** A new unit test in the same file feeds a fixture copy of the core doc with section headings renamed (e.g. `## Authoring seams (content, manifest, validator, author)` → `## Renamed seam section`) and asserts the contract check still passes; a negative fixture (missing `createStorylineSystem`) asserts the check still fails. *Metric: run the two fixture cases — tolerance passes, regression fails.*
- **AC3 — Link resolution preserved.** The guard keeps asserting that `docs/game/storylines.md` links to `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md` and that the target resolves on disk, and that the core reference is linked from `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `core/docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md`.
- **AC4 — Failure messages and rationale.** Any guard failure names the offending file and the missing anchor, and the test header comment explains that engine doc headings are not a cross-repo contract and cites this work item (`MS-0MVMNO29Z009SF6O`); a corresponding one-line note is added near the "thin adapters" paragraph of `docs/game/storylines.md` and under the `## Tests` heading in `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` so the next engineer does not re-pin headings. *Metric: a reading of the header comment + both doc notes shows the work-item id and the "headings are not a contract" statement.*
- **AC5 — Engine-revision tolerant and suite green.** The changed test scope passes with the submodule at the pinned SHA and with the engine dev tip the build composes; the full project test suite passes with the change.

## Constraints

- Game-side change only — do **not** edit files inside `core/` (engine-owned submodule, re-scaffolded by the game-repo scaffold); if an engine-side fix is later chosen, it is an engine-repo (CG) work item.
- Do not weaken the guard into a no-op: negative cases (missing file, missing symbol, broken link) must still fail the suite.
- No new dependencies; keep the guard in plain vitest + `node:fs`, consistent with the file's existing style.
- Do not change `configs/engine-pin.json` or the `core` gitlink as part of this work (they already agree at dev HEAD: pin `40f83b986a6578b3887dcda8857dd5ee7aa15e57` == gitlink `40f83b98`, re-pinned by commit `5b2ddf72`; the pair moves together on every dev build, so treat the exact SHA as illustrative, not a constant).

## Existing state

- Guard: `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts`, AC5b block asserts `['## API', '## Authoring seams', '## UI adapter', '## Gym demo']` against `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md` (created by MS-0MUMP968H005MXZY / MS-0MVFMA9EW001MIQR; heading pin baked in by commit `9f2c6185`).
- Engine doc at current pin (`40f83b98`) has sections: API, Validation, Authoring seams (content, manifest, validator, author), Editor (visual authoring tool), Engine adapter, UI adapter, Gym demo, Testing. Note both `## Authoring seams …` and `## Engine adapter` exist at this revision — proof that pinning either name is fragile; the guard must not depend on heading text at all.
- The engine repo currently has **no** docs-consistency test and **no** heading anchor manifest (verified: no engine tests reference `docs/core-engine`, no anchor file) — so "engine owns the contract" would be net-new engine work.
- Sibling churn pattern already fixed inline: MS-0MVMOH2N3000T63F (pin/pointer mismatch when dev sync advances the submodule during a build).

## Desired change

1. Refactor the AC5b assertions into a small pure helper `checkCoreReferenceContract(coreDoc: string, headers: {file: string; link: boolean}): string[]` (returns missing anchors), so the same logic runs against the real file and against fixtures.
2. Replace the `['## API', …]` heading pins with: file-exists + `createStorylineSystem`/`@story-line`/`GymStorylineScene` presence + a structural check that the doc "documents the section topics" without pinning exact heading text (e.g. each required topic keyword found somewhere in the doc, tolerant of heading renames).
3. Add fixture-driven tests for rename tolerance (pass) and missing-symbol regression (fail).
4. Update the test header comment + the two doc notes (AC4).

## Implementation plan (single vertical slice)

This is a **leaf `task`**, not an epic: one test file plus two one-line doc notes. It is
small enough (effort `Small`, risk `Medium`) that phasing adds ceremony without value, so it is
implemented as a **single vertical slice** (code/guard + tests + docs in one change set) rather
than decomposed into child work items. Within that slice the order preserves test-first
verification: the new contract check is written so its tolerance/regression fixtures fail before
the old heading pins are removed, then the pins are replaced, then the docs notes land.

1. Extract the AC5b assertions into `checkCoreReferenceContract(coreDoc, headers)` returning a
   list of missing anchors (pure, no `fs` inside) — AC1 groundwork, keeps the real-file and
   fixture paths on the same logic.
2. Add the fixture tests first and watch them fail against the current heading-pinned helper:
   renamed-heading fixture passes, `createStorylineSystem`-missing fixture fails — AC2.
3. Replace the `['## API', …]` pins with file-exists + `createStorylineSystem` / `@story-line` /
   `GymStorylineScene` + rename-tolerant section-topic check, calling the helper — AC1, AC3.
4. Update the header comment and the two doc notes with the work-item id — AC4.
5. Verify with the changed-scope test run at the current checkout, then the full suite — AC5.
6. Finish with the standard implementation close-out (build → test → commit in that order).

## Key Files

- `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts` — AC5b block rewrite, tolerance/regression fixture tests, header rationale.
- `tests/main-street/fixtures/storyline-core-doc-renamed-heading.md` (new) — fixture mirroring the current core doc with headings renamed; or an inline string fixture to avoid duplicating a 400-line doc. Prefer the smallest fixture that provably exercises the renames; if inline, note that it must be refreshed on engine doc content changes.
- `docs/game/storylines.md` — one-line note that the guard asserts semantic anchors, not engine heading text.
- `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` — one-line note under "Tests" about the engine-doc heading non-contract.
- `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md`, `configs/engine-pin.json`, `core` gitlink — read-only references; must not be edited here.

## Related work

- MS-0MVFMA9EW001MIQR — created AC5b ("Storyline docs and drift guards", completed).
- MS-0MUMP968H005MXZY — canonical docs + doc-drift guard (completed).

# Main Street story-line adapter does not apply option cost/extraEffect

**Headline:** The Main Street story-line engine adapter omits the core `applyResourceDelta` seam, so option `cost` and `extraEffect` are never charged or applied.

Discovered-from: `MS-0MVI0APQY000OIOY` (cost-aware event-choice over the core presented option list).

## Problem

Core `@story-line` resolves an option's declarative `cost` and `extraEffect` through the engine adapter's optional `applyResourceDelta` seam (`core/src/story-line/resolve.ts`). A legacy adapter without it is left untouched and appends the activity-log line *"Story-line cost/extra-effect not applied: the engine adapter does not implement applyResourceDelta."*

`mainStreetStorylineEngineAdapter` (`src/MainStreetStorylineAdapter.ts`) implements `rng`, `applyEffect`, `getResources`, `appendLog`, `getActivityLog`, `getTemplate`, `getBaseTypeId`, `getChainScanCards` and `pushChainCard` — but **not** `applyResourceDelta`.

Consequences:

- A cost-gated option is filtered out of the presented list at draw time (`isOptionAffordable`), yet a *presented* cost option is never actually charged — so affordability never changes after paying.
- `extraEffect` deltas silently never land (options are inert where content expects a bonus/penalty).
- Any card using a cost or extra effect pollutes the activity log with the warning line above.

## Impact

Until this is fixed, the AI cost-aware policy (`MS-0MVI0APQY000OIOY`) scores costs that the engine never collects and effects that never apply. The AI unit contract can still be satisfied (projection is a pure function), but end-to-end play with cost-bearing options is incorrect.

Secondary gap (same story, narrower): CSV `options` authoring has no syntax for `cost`/`extraEffect`, and `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json` `#/definitions/option` carries only `label`/`successorIds`/`effectPolicy`. So content cannot yet declare a cost — only registered options can. Authoring support should be its own item once enforcement exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `mainStreetStorylineEngineAdapter` implements `applyResourceDelta(state, delta)`, applying `coins` and `reputation` deltas to `state.resourceBank` and keeping the ledger/score view consistent (same sync path `resolveEventOption` uses, e.g. `syncResourceBankToLedger`).
- A unit test proves a cost-bearing option deducts exactly `cost.coins`/`cost.reputation` on resolution, for both `effectPolicy: 'apply'` and `'skip'`.
- A unit test proves `extraEffect` deltas are applied for both effect policies, and that the resolution result's `coinChange`/`repChange` reports cost + extra effect + (for `apply`) the card effect.
- An integration test resolves a pending cost choice headlessly and asserts the activity log contains **no** "Story-line cost/extra-effect not applied" line.
- Undo of a resolved paid choice (snapshot command) restores the pre-payment resources; save/load round-trip preserves the post-payment balance.
- Existing behaviour with cost-free options is unchanged (storyline regression harness green).

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `applyResourceDelta` to the adapter, delegating to the existing state resource helpers and the ledger sync one-liner.
- Follow the settlement order documented in core: card effect (per `effectPolicy`) → cost → extra effect.

## Key Files:

- `src/MainStreetStorylineAdapter.ts` — add `applyResourceDelta`
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `resolveEventOption` settlement/ledger sync + log assertions
- `src/MainStreetState.ts` — `resourceBank` and ledger sync helpers
- `core/src/story-line/resolve.ts` — settlement order and warning contract (read-only)
- `tests/main-street/storyline-model.test.ts` — resolution test home

## Notes

- `core/` is a pinned submodule — no core changes expected; if core needs a signature change, raise it as a core (`CG-`) item instead.

# Intake Brief — End of Turn summary dialog for competitive mode (MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI)

## Problem statement

The single-player End of Turn summary dialog (MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41) gives the
player a deliberate review-and-advance moment after each turn. Competitive
(human-vs-AI) play has no equivalent: after the shared day's closing
presentation (`presentCompetitiveClosing`) the day auto-advances with only the
transient per-seat income text (`Player 1: +X coins | Player 2: +Y coins`, via
`perSeatClosingSummary`) and the incident reveal. There is no moment to compare
each seat's standing for the round just completed — businesses owned, income
and expenses per seat. This item extends the End of Turn summary dialog to
competitive mode: one panel per completed round (one shared day where every
seat finished and the closing ran), with **owner-keyed rows** (businesses
owned, income/expenses per seat).

## Users

- **Main Street competitive player (human seat)** — plays week-by-week against
  AI seats on the shared street; after each shared day's animations finish,
  wants a persistent panel showing every seat's round result and a deliberate
  "start the next day" action (parity with the single-player dialog).

**User stories:**

- As a competitive player, when the shared day's closing animations finish, I
  see one panel summarising the round with a row per seat (businesses owned,
  income, expenses, net change, closing coins/reputation/score) so I can
  compare standings and learn from the round.
- As a competitive player, I click **[ Next Turn ]** to start the next shared
  day — the day does not advance until I do.
- As a competitive player, I see the same (disabled) **[ Bank Loan ]**
  affordance as the single-player dialog, so the loans option is planned and
  consistent across modes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In competitive play (N ≥ 2), after the shared closing presentation
   completes, a Turn Summary dialog appears with one panel per completed round
   — one owner-keyed row per non-eliminated seat showing businesses owned,
   income (with the per-phase breakdown), ongoing expenses per category
   (staff / community / business), net coin change, and closing coins /
   reputation / score. The next shared day does **not** start until the player
   clicks **[ Next Turn ]**. Reduced-motion, replay and headless/AI-driven
   paths skip the dialog and keep the existing auto-advance pacing.
2. The dialog content is **engine-computed and owner-keyed**: the competitive
   close surfaces per-seat ongoing costs, businesses owned and net change on
   `TurnResult` (extending the parent item's owner-keyed ledger design), so
   every value shown is testable without a browser and consistent with the
   single-player ledger. Additions are optional/backwards-compatible —
   `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn`, `presentCompetitiveClosing` and the
   headless/Monte-Carlo paths are unaffected when the field is absent.
3. The dialog reuses the single-player Turn Summary presentation: the
   Phaser-free model renders owner-keyed rows (reusing the competitive
   scoreboard's `You`/`AI n` labels and `resolveSeatColour` seat colours);
   **[ Next Turn ]** (primary) and **[ Bank Loan ]** (**disabled** with an
   explanatory hint, behind the same single wiring seam that
   MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG replaces — never enabled by this item) buttons; overlay
   conventions: `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton`, elements in
   `s.hudContainer`, depths 199/200/201, pushed into `s.overlayObjects`,
   `safePlaySound` for the button SFX.
4. Single-player behaviour is unchanged; the competitive gate slots only in
   the scene presentation tail — between `presentCompetitiveClosing` completing
   and `startTurnPhase` in `presentCompetitiveDayTail` — and never in the
   engine/headless close path. Checkpoint save ordering
   (`presentCompetitiveDayTail` saves before the closing) is unchanged; the
   dialog adds no save and mutates no state.
5. At least one automated test per surfaced value (Phaser-free model tests for
   owner-keyed rows, engine per-seat ledger tests, and a competitive-mode
   browser dialog test); **all related documentation is updated**
   (docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md competitive closing section and the end-of-turn
   summary section, plus any README/dev references); **the full project test
   suite passes** with the changes.

## Constraints

- **Blocked-by MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** (outbound dependency): the parent item is
  still `open` (stage `intake_complete`) — its `TurnResult` owner-keyed ledger
  does **not exist in the code yet**. This item builds on and consumes that
  ledger; implementers must land/coordinate with the parent first. Per-seat
  expense capture does not exist anywhere today — `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`
  returns `void` and only logs — so the per-seat ledger extension is real
  engine work on top of the parent's ledger shape (kept optional and
  backwards-compatible throughout).
- Presentation-only contract: the dialog reads committed state / `result` and
  never mutates engine state or consumes RNG. In competitive, deltas are
  already applied to each `PlayerRecord` before the closing is presented, so
  the panel shows post-round values; the checkpoint save stays in
  `presentCompetitiveDayTail` (existing ordering).
- Overlay conventions (AGENTS.md UI best practices) exactly as the parent
  item constrains: `createOverlayBackground` + `createOverlayButton` from
  `@ui`; elements parented into `s.hudContainer`; depths 199 / 200 / 201;
  everything pushed into `s.overlayObjects` for dismissal; instant appearance
  (reduced-motion safe); button SFX via `safePlaySound`.
- Headless determinism and bounded pacing must not regress: Monte-Carlo /
  AI headless days (`MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts`, `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn`)
  never invoke the scene presentation and must never show/block on the dialog;
  the competitive closing bound (`COMPETITIVE_CLOSING_MAX_TOTAL_MS`) stays.
- **Assumption (Q-scope, from repo evidence):** a "round" equals **one
  completed shared day** — all non-eliminated seats finished and the shared

  day (`round-robin` seat iteration only), so "one panel per completed round"

- **Assumption (blocking safety):** competitive is human-vs-AI on one device

## Existing state

  `income.phaseBreakdown.perSlotBreakdown` (base / synergy / reputation /

  business running costs per slot owner via `ownerTaggedGrid` — but are
  **not surfaced** on any result (void, log-only). Businesses owned per seat

  (`src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts`).
- Per-seat row conventions exist in `buildCompetitiveScoreboard`
  (`src/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScoreboard.ts`): `You` / `AI n` labels,
  `resolveSeatColour` seat colours, coin/rep/score columns — reused by the

# Wire Bank Loan button into the Turn Summary dialog

Follow-up raised by the Bank Loans planning session (MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG), per producer
decision Q4: the Turn Summary dialog (MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41) has landed, so its deliberately
disabled **Bank Loan** affordance can now be wired to the loan feature.

## Problem statement

The Turn Summary dialog shows an always-disabled **[ Bank Loan ]** button and never calls
the `onBankLoanAction` seam reserved for the loans feature, so a mid-game player has no
entry point to credit at all — the loan engine only surfaces offers on bankruptcy. This item
turns the reserved affordance into a working mid-game loan entry point, with no new engine
rules.

## Users

- **Mid-game human player (single-player)** — "When the Turn Summary dialog is on screen
  and I am short of cash, I want to borrow from the configured loan menu so I can fund the
  next week's move, and I want to see the repayment schedule before I commit."
- **Cautious player** — "I want the button to tell me *why* it is unavailable (loans turned
  off, or I already owe money) instead of a generic 'coming soon' note."

Not a user of this slice: competitive seats (per-seat closing text, no summary dialog),
AI seats (bailout-only policy — no proactive loans).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Enabled/disabled matrix.** The Bank Loan button is interactive only when
   `state.config.loansEnabled === true` **and** the acting (human) seat holds no active loan;
   in every other case it is rendered disabled (muted, `input` disabled) with a hint that
   explains the reason.
2. **Selector with schedule.** Pressing the enabled button opens the loan selector listing
   every configured `config.loanOptions` entry with its per-turn repayment and total
   repayment, plus a way to back out; backing out returns to the Turn Summary dialog with no
   state change.
3. **Confirm dispatches `takeLoan`.** Confirming an option dispatches the `takeLoan` command
   for the acting seat, credits the principal to that seat's wallet, records the active loan,
   and leaves `actionsRemaining` unchanged.
4. **No day advance.** Neither opening the selector nor confirming a loan advances the day or
   resumes the deferred closing; the day advances only on **[ Next Turn ]**, exactly once.
5. **Refreshed dialog.** After the loan is taken the Turn Summary dialog is re-rendered from
   the same `TurnResult` with the post-`takeLoan` state, so the new obligation is visible and
   the button is now disabled (one-active-loan rule) while **[ Next Turn ]** still works.
6. **Testing/validation.** Tests cover the enabled/disabled matrix (loans enabled + no loan,
   active loan, `loansEnabled: false`), the selector content, the `takeLoan` dispatch, the
   no-action-point rule, the cancel path, and that the day does not advance before
   **[ Next Turn ]**.
7. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments (`showTurnSummaryDialog`, the gate, the button-construction site),
   `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (the "[ Bank Loan ] is always disabled" paragraph), and the
   in-game help/loan documentation touched by MS-0MVPWSFDN000QJXB.
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — `showTurnSummaryDialog(summary, onNextTurn,
  onBankLoanAction?)` renders `[ Bank Loan ]` with `disableInteractive()`, colour
  `#6b6459`, and the hint *“Bank loans are not available yet — coming in a future update.”*;
  it explicitly does `void onBankLoanAction` so the seam can never fire. `BANK_LOAN_HINT` is
  duplicated in `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts`, whose AC4 asserts
  "always disabled, seam never invoked" — that test must be rewritten, not deleted.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — `showTurnSummaryDialog(summary, onNextTurn,
  onBankLoanAction?)` delegates to `msOverlayManager`; with no overlay manager (headless) it
  calls `onNextTurn()` immediately so the closing is never stranded.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — `shouldGateTurnSummary()` restricts the
  dialog to `requiresDeferredClosing` single-player closings (never replay, reduced motion,
  tutorial or competitive); `presentTurnSummaryGate()` builds the summary with
  `buildTurnSummary(s.state, result)` and calls
  `s.showTurnSummaryDialog(summary, onNextTurn)` — the third argument is not passed today.
- Overlays already read live state (`s.state.config` in `MainStreetOverlayContent`), so
  `loansEnabled` needs no new plumbing into the scene.
- `buildTurnSummary()` is Phaser-free and read-only, so re-rendering after a loan only needs
  the same `state` + `result` pair re-run.
- **The loan engine does not exist yet.** `src/MainStreetLoans.ts`, `config.loansEnabled`,
  `config.loanOptions`, the `takeLoan` command and `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` are
  all still unimplemented: the Bank Loans epic MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG sits at
  `intake_complete`, its slices are `blocked` (only the headless determinism baseline,
  MS-0MVPWS45N008PR0X, is in flight). This item is the epic's only out-of-epic follow-up and
  must land *after* the model, `takeLoan`, and overlay-UI slices.
- Save schema v3 (loans + pending offer) is delivered by the epic; this slice must not touch
  serialisation.

## Desired change

1. **Carry a loans descriptor into the dialog.** Extend the gate's call so the dialog receives
   one small Phaser-free descriptor rather than reaching into scene state ad hoc — predicted
   shape `{ enabled: boolean; activeLoan: { perTurnRepayment, turnsRemaining } | null;
   options: LoanOption[] }` built in `presentTurnSummaryGate()` from `s.state.config` and the
   acting seat. Keeps the overlay presentation-only and the descriptor unit-testable.
   (Implementation may instead read `s.state` directly if the epic's helpers make that
   cleaner — the ACs do not care which; see Assumptions.)
2. **Enable the affordance** when `enabled && activeLoan === null`, wiring `pointerdown` to
   the `onBankLoanAction` seam; keep the button disabled otherwise with a reason-specific
   hint (loans disabled vs. already owing — see open question Q3).
3. **Loan selector** presented on press: reuse the epic's `MainStreetLoanOverlay` option rows
   (per-turn + total repayment). The epic builds it for a *pending offer* driven by
   `state.pendingLoanOffer`; this slice needs a non-bailout mode (no pending offer, options
   from `config.loanOptions`, Cancel/back instead of Decline). Reusing the row renderer, not
   duplicating it, is the requirement; a small `mode` parameter is expected.
4. **Confirm = dispatch.** Confirming dispatches the `takeLoan` command through the existing
   command surface (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts`), never mutating state inline.
5. **Refresh in place** after a successful take: rebuild the summary from the same
   `TurnResult` and re-render the dialog (dismiss the old overlay objects first so
   `s.overlayObjects` stays consistent), leaving `[ Next Turn ]` as the only way to resume
   `advanceTurn`.
6. **Tests** in a new `tests/main-street/turn-summary-bank-loan.browser.test.ts` (browser
   overlay, mirroring `turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts` helpers) plus the rewrite of the
   dialog suite's AC4 case.

## Constraints

- **Presentation wiring only** — no new engine rules, no changes to the loan model, repayment
  maths or one-active-loan validation; those belong to MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG.
- **No action point cost** and **no day advance** — taking a loan from the dialog must leave
  `actionsRemaining` untouched and must not resume the deferred closing.
- **Single-player deferred path only** — the dialog itself is gated to that path; competitive
  per-seat closing and the tutorial/reduced-motion/replay paths are unchanged.
- **Overlay conventions** (`core` UI best practices): `createOverlayBackground` +
  `createOverlayButton`, all elements parented into `s.hudContainer` and pushed to
  `s.overlayObjects`, depths 199/200/201, instant appearance (reduced-motion safe), SFX via
  `safePlaySound`.
- **Blocked-by sequencing** — depends on MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG (dependency edge already
  recorded): specifically the loan model/config slice (MS-0MVPWS5JB007YSHB), the `takeLoan`
  command slice (MS-0MVPWS6WB008WP79) and the overlay-UI slice (MS-0MVPWSBLG006YMBA).

## Assumptions

- **A1 First repayment falls on the next turn's closing.** The closing sequence (and its
  ledger) has already run when the dialog is presented, so a loan taken at the dialog must not
  charge a repayment against the turn being summarised. Recorded as OPEN QUESTION Q1 for
  producer confirmation.
- **A2 Proactive loans are allowed at any coin balance** — the button is not gated on
  affordability or negative coins (the goal is mid-game credit, not a second bailout path).
- **A3 The selector's rows come from `config.loanOptions`**, so a re-balanced menu needs no UI
  change, and the dialog is unavailable (button disabled) when the menu is empty.
- **A4 `takeLoan` rejection is surfaced, not swallowed** — if the engine refuses (e.g. a race
  into an active loan), the dialog shows the engine's reason and stays open rather than
  silently closing.
- **A5 Headless safety is untouched** — with no overlay manager the scene still calls
  `onNextTurn()`; the new descriptor must remain optional so existing call sites compile.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Sequencing risk (highest):** the epic is not implemented; starting this slice early would
  mean inventing engine helpers (scope creep). Mitigation: keep the item dependency-blocked
  until the three prerequisites are `completed`.
- **Duplicated overlay logic:** copy-pasting the bailout overlay instead of parameterising it
  would leave two loan selectors to maintain. Mitigation: AC2/desired-change 3 require reusing
  the epic's row renderer.
- **Stale dialog content:** re-rendering from a mutated `state` but a stale `TurnResult` can
  show a mismatch. Mitigation: rebuild via `buildTurnSummary(state, result)` with the same
  `result` object (the ledger is presentation data, not recomputed).
- **Overlay object leak:** dismissing and re-rendering must reset `s.overlayObjects` the same
  way `dismissOverlay` does, or duplicated buttons accumulate in `hudContainer`. Mitigation:
  explicit test asserting a single `[ Next Turn ]`/`[ Bank Loan ]` pair after a refresh.
- **Test drift:** `turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts` AC4 encodes "always disabled"; leaving
  it untouched makes the suite self-contradictory. Mitigation: rewrite that case in the same
  commit.
- **Scope creep:** competitive-mode parity (MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI), AI proactive loans, multiple
  loans, loan repayment UI polish — record as linked work items, do not fold in.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — enable/disable `[ Bank Loan ]`, wire the seam,
  render the reason-specific hint and refresh the dialog after a take.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — build and pass the loans descriptor in
  `presentTurnSummaryGate()`; keep `shouldGateTurnSummary()` unchanged.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — pass the descriptor through the delegation method.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` — reuse the epic's option rows in a non-bailout
  (mid-game select) mode.
- `src/MainStreetLoans.ts` — consume `activeLoanFor` / option-table helpers (read-only use).
- `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — `takeLoan` command dispatch and the no-AP assertion.
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-bank-loan.browser.test.ts` — **new.** Wiring tests.
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts` — rewrite the "seam never invoked"
  case.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — update the "always disabled" Turn Summary paragraph.

## Out of scope / non-goals

- Competitive-mode summary dialog and any competitive loan entry point
  (MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI).
- Engine rules: repayment timing, bailout offer loop, AI policy, persistence — owned by
  MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG.
- HUD obligation readout (MS-0MVPWSCRD004A6Z4) and the loans help/documentation slice
  (MS-0MVPWSFDN000QJXB); this item only edits the one doc paragraph it invalidates.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG** (Bank Loans, epic, `intake_complete`) — the engine this slice wires
  into; dependency edge recorded.
- **MS-0MVPWS5JB007YSHB** (Loan model, config and repayment maths), **MS-0MVPWS6WB008WP79**
  (`takeLoan` command and one-active-loan rule), **MS-0MVPWSBLG006YMBA** (Bailout overlay UI
  and deferred closing resume) — prerequisites.
- **MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** (End of Turn summary, completed) — parent of the dialog; its AC
  anticipated the Bank Loan button.
- **MS-0MVP46AMO002SZUT** (Overlay: turn summary dialog + browser test, completed) — created
  the disabled affordance and its `onBankLoanAction` seam.
- **MS-0MVP46Q8X003419R** (deferred closing gate, completed) — the gate that presents the
  dialog; see `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` § "Turn Summary dialog and the closing gate".
- **MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI** (End of Turn summary dialog for competitive mode, open) — the other
  mode's dialog; explicitly not covered here.
- Repo: `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`,
  `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`, `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts`,
  `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (repayment timing): "A loan taken from the Turn Summary dialog — when does the first
  repayment hit? (A) at the next turn's closing, since this turn's closing and ledger have
  already run [recommended]; (B) immediately when the deferred closing resumes, so the turn
  just summarised carries it; (C) other." — **OPEN QUESTION.** No answer yet; the item is
  blocked by the epic anyway. Draft assumes **A** (see Assumption A1). Source: raised in the
  intake session 2026-10-27, no interactive producer available (auto-dispatched downtime run).
- Q2 (mode scope): "Should the enabled button also cover any non-single-player summary
  surface? (A) no — single-player deferred path only; competitive parity stays with
  MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI [recommended]; (B) cover competitive too." — **OPEN QUESTION**, draft
  assumes **A** (already consistent with `shouldGateTurnSummary`).
- Q3 (disabled hint wording): "When the seat already holds an active loan, what should the
  disabled hint say? (A) show the outstanding obligation, e.g. *'Active loan: 110 coins/week,
  4 weeks left.'* [recommended]; (B) a generic *'You already have an active loan.'*; (C) keep
  the current generic text." — **OPEN QUESTION**, draft assumes **A**.
- Q4 (proactive eligibility): "Is the button available at any balance, or only when the seat
  cannot cover its costs?" — answered from the seed goal (mid-game credit use case): **any
  balance**, recorded as Assumption A2. Source: work-item description "As a mid-game player …
  I can click [ Bank Loan ]".
- Q5 (selector reuse): "Does the epic's bailout overlay support a non-bailout option list?" —
  research: `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` does not exist yet; the epic's Key Files
  predict it as the pending-offer overlay. Draft therefore requires a reuse with a mode
  parameter rather than a copy (Risks: duplicated overlay logic). Source: `wl show
  MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG --json`, `ls src/scenes/`.
- Q6 (dependency): "Is the loan engine available to wire against?" — research: no — `grep -ri
  loan src` returns only the dialog's placeholder comments; the epic is at `intake_complete`
  with its slices `blocked`. Recorded as a hard prerequisite. Source: repo grep, `wl search
  loan --json`.
## Related work (automated report)

- **MS-0MVP46AMO002SZUT** – Overlay: turn summary dialog + browser test (completed)
- **MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** – End of Turn summary. When all animations for the End of Turn phase have completed we should pop up a dialog with details of the current state of the game. # of businesses owned by each player, income and expenses for that turn, one-off income/expenses (from events etc.) and any other information that would be useful and informative. The dialog will have a "next turn" button and a "Bank Loan" button which will allow them to take out a loan (a feature not yet implemented, see work item) (completed)

# Intake Brief — Reputation is no longer represented by people walking the streets (MS-0MVRDVVH4001048Q)

**Type:** bug (regression) · **Priority:** high · **Stage:** intake

## Headline

The ambient reputation crowd is missing again: the pedestrian silhouette layer shipped in v0.1.19 no longer appears on the street in normal play, so reputation has lost its diegetic on-street presence and the reputation income no longer visibly comes from the people in the shops.

## Problem statement

Reputation used to be represented by a live crowd of small silhouettes that walked the roads and entered occupied businesses; those figures scaled with reputation and sourced the end-of-turn reputation income. The producer reports a regression: the crowd is gone. The layer source and its scene/renderer/turn-flow hooks are still present in `dev`, so the regression is most likely in scene integration or rendering (attach/rebuild ordering, camera/mask, HUD refresh path, reducers that gate rendering, or a layout change that moves the layer off-screen) rather than the feature having been deleted.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — wants to see their reputation as a living street: more reputation means a busier street, and the end-of-turn reputation income visibly comes from the people in their shops.
  - *As a player, I want the street to show how reputable I have become, so progress is legible without reading the HUD.*
  - *As a player, I want the people in my shops to be the source of my reputation income, so the economy feels diegetic.*
- **Producer / game designer** — wants the shipped behaviour restored exactly as documented, not redesigned, and wants a guard so this regression cannot silently return.
- **Developer / QA** — needs the layer to stay presentation-only, deterministic, reduced-motion/replay exempt, and non-blocking, and needs a scene-level test that would have caught the disappearance.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Regression reproduced and root cause recorded.** The work item records a concrete reproduction (mode, difficulty, steps, build/commit) and the change or condition that made the crowd disappear — the offending commit/file where one exists, or the ruled-out alternatives and the failing condition where it does not. The fix commit references that finding. Verified by reading the work-item comment and the fix commit message.
2. **Crowd is visible in normal play.** On a fresh normal-play game (default settings, not Reduced Motion, not replay/headless), once the HUD has rendered the player's starting reputation the street displays `pedestrianCount(state.resourceBank.reputation)` silhouette figures in `PEDESTRIAN_COLOR`, parented to the live street container. Verified by a scene-level browser/behaviour test that boots the real scene and asserts the layer's live figure count equals the pure helper and that the layer container is attached to the current street container with non-empty, on-screen bounds.
3. **Live population reconciliation still holds.** A reputation gain during a turn fades a figure in and a loss fades a figure out, delta-only, so the on-street count always tracks the HUD reputation value. Verified by the existing live-refresh test plus a scene-level assertion that the count is non-zero and matches `pedestrianCount(reputation)` after the first HUD refresh.
4. **Figures walk the roads and enter occupied businesses.** The documented road-lane walking, nearest-occupied-cell targeting, deliberate (non-teleporting) shop entry and crowd persistence across a street rebuild are retained. Verified by the existing pure/behaviour tests staying green and by a regression assertion that, by the reputation income phase, at least `PEDESTRIAN_MIN_SHOP_RATIO` (25%) of the live crowd is inside occupied cells.
5. **Reputation income is sourced from the crowd.** The `reputation` income phase keeps sourcing each business's coin flight from a figure inside that business (then a figure entering it, then any shopper, then a street anchor — never the HUD reputation counter), with the credited total unchanged. Verified by the existing income-phase source/invariant tests.
6. **Exemptions and determinism preserved.** Reduced Motion and replay/headless modes render no figures, no dissolve and no flights; the layer consumes no gameplay RNG (only the presentation-local PRNG) and a throwing layer never stalls the turn. Verified by existing exemption/determinism tests.
7. **Regression guard added.** A test that fails while the crowd is absent (e.g. a scene-level assertion of a non-empty, attached, visible layer at game start in normal play) is added so a future change cannot silently remove the crowd again. Verified by the new test failing on the pre-fix commit and passing on the fix.
8. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Restore, do not redesign.** The intended behaviour is the one documented in `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` § "Ambient street pedestrians" and delivered by `MS-0MTV9AS15004AC1E`; the fix restores it rather than introducing a new crowd design, ratio or choreography.
- **Presentation-only.** The layer and its dissolve must never mutate game state, the transcript or the turn flow; every entry point stays defensive so a bad frame cannot stall a turn.
- **No economy change.** Credited reputation income, the phase-sum invariant and the deferred-mutation handling are untouched.
- **Reduced Motion + replay/headless exemption** remain mandatory.
- **No new gameplay RNG consumption.** Any randomness stays in the presentation-local PRNG.
- **Minimal churn.** Touch only the pedestrian layer and the integration point(s) that caused the regression; do not undo unrelated panel/layout work.
- **Respect repository boundaries.** If the root cause is in the `core` submodule or shared UI, raise a separate core work item and record the dependency rather than editing the submodule silently.

## Existing state

- The feature exists and is wired in `dev`:
  - `src/scenes/MainStreetPedestrians.ts` — the layer (`pedestrianCount`, `buildRoadNetwork`, road-lane walking, shop entry, `startNewTurn`, `beginEndOfTurn`, `dissolveIntoCoins`, `setPopulation`, `update`).
  - `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` — constructs the layer, destroys it on shutdown and re-clamps it on resize.
  - `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — re-attaches the layer at the end of `refreshStreetGrid` after `streetContainer.removeAll(true)`.
  - `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — drives `msPedestrians.update(delta)` from the scene `update` loop.
  - `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts` — `animateHudValueChanges` reconciles the population to `pedestrianCount(reputation)`; `dissolveReputationCoins` sources the reputation phase from the layer.
  - `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — `startNewTurn()` on a new day and `beginEndOfTurn()` at end of turn.
- The feature shipped in **v0.1.19** (epic `MS-0MTV9AS15004AC1E`, children listed under Related work).
- Documentation: `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` § "Ambient street pedestrians (reputation crowd)" describes the population rule, road walking, shop entry, live refresh, turn lifecycle, income conversion, accessibility and performance.
- The source file is unchanged since v0.1.19, so the regression is expected at an integration point changed after that release.

### Candidate causes to check (investigation starting points, not conclusions)

- **Attach/rebuild ordering:** `refreshStreetGrid` calls `streetContainer.removeAll(true)` (which destroys the layer's container) and re-attaches at the end; a new early return or reordering after v0.1.19 would leave the crowd destroyed.
- **Scene lifecycle:** the layer is re-created in two places in `createScene`; a second construction or a new boot path (new-game overlay, tutorial offer, checkpoint resume) may leave the live instance with `targetCount = 0`.
- **HUD refresh path:** the population is only reconciled from `animateHudValueChanges`; a change that bypasses, early-returns or defers that path (e.g. the display-only counting work) would stop `setPopulation` from running.
- **Render gating:** `isEnabled()` returns false when `replayMode` or `settingsPanel.reducedMotion` is true; a settings default change or a mis-detected replay mode would hide the layer.
- **Camera/mask/layout:** pedestrians are map-local children of the masked, camera-transformed street container; a layout, zoom or mask change can move or clip them off-screen while the slots stay visible.
- **Layer stacking:** the "UI simplification when roads are visible" epic made the market, hand and HUD panels opaque and moved the hand band; the crowd may be present but hidden behind a panel rather than absent.
- **End-of-turn timing:** the Turn Summary gate now defers the next day until **[ Next Turn ]**; during that dialog the crowd has already walked off the block, so "empty street" between turns is expected and must be distinguished from an empty street during a turn.

## Desired change

- Diagnose and fix the regression so the ambient reputation crowd is visible during normal play and the documented behaviour (road walking, shop entry, live reconciliation, crowd-sourced reputation income) is restored.
- Add the scene-level regression guard from AC7 so the layer cannot silently disappear again.
- Record the root cause and the guard in the work item and, where the documentation was thin on the lifecycle/attach contract, tighten `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (or add a short note in `src/scenes/README.md`) so the next renderer change has a visible contract.
- Leave the economy, panel treatment, turn pacing and accessibility behaviour untouched.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetPedestrians.ts` — the layer; likely unchanged except a defensive fix if the root cause is in the layer.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — `refreshStreetGrid` attach ordering / early returns; prime suspect for a rebuild-time disappearance.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — scene `update` loop and `getStreetContainer`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` — construction/re-construction, shutdown, resize.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts` — `syncPedestrianPopulation` / `animateHudValueChanges` / `dissolveReputationCoins`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorContext.ts` — animator accessors used by the dissolve path.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — `startNewTurn` / `beginEndOfTurn` hooks and the Turn Summary gate.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — pedestrian constants (ratio, colour, size, speed, fade, shop ratio).
- `src/MainStreetMapView.ts` — road bands, viewport rect and camera transform used to place the layer.
- `tests/main-street/pedestrians-layer.test.ts` — pure/behaviour coverage of the layer.
- `tests/main-street/pedestrians-live-refresh.test.ts` — live reconciliation coverage.
- `tests/main-street/pedestrians-count.test.ts` — population rule.
